title: From Avoidant to Secure: Opening Your Heart to Connection
summary: A comprehensive seven-module CBT program designed to help you transform avoidant attachment patterns into secure attachment. Learn to recognize and express emotions, build intimacy, trust others, communicate vulnerably, and develop the secure attachment style that allows for both independence and deep connection.

modules.title: Module 1 • Understanding Avoidant Attachment: The Foundation
modules.overview: Avoidant attachment isn't a flaw—it's a learned pattern of self-protection that developed to keep you safe. Understanding this pattern is the first step toward transforming it. This module helps you understand how avoidant attachment develops, recognize its characteristics in your relationships, and see the path toward secure attachment. Knowledge is power. When you understand your attachment style, you can begin to change it. This module gives you that foundation.
takeaways: Avoidant attachment is a learned pattern, not a character flaw—it can be changed.
Understanding your attachment style helps you recognize patterns and make different choices.
Secure attachment is achievable—you can learn to be both independent and connected.
Self-awareness is the first step: noticing your patterns without judgment.
exercises: Attachment style reflection: Write about your earliest memories of seeking comfort or connection. What happened? How did you learn to cope?
Pattern identification: List 5 behaviors or thoughts you have in relationships that might relate to avoidant attachment.
Relationship timeline: Create a timeline of your significant relationships. What patterns do you see? How has avoidant attachment shown up?
homework: Attachment journal: For one week, journal about your relationship thoughts and feelings. Notice when you withdraw. What triggers it?
Pattern observation: This week, observe your avoidant attachment patterns without judgment. Just notice. What do you see?
Secure attachment vision: Write about what secure attachment would look like for you. What would change? How would you feel?
Self-compassion practice: When you notice avoidant patterns, practice self-compassion. 'This is a learned pattern. I'm learning to change it. That's okay.'

modules.title: Module 2 • Building Emotional Awareness: Reconnecting with Your Feelings
modules.overview: Avoidant attachment often involves suppressing or dismissing emotions. This module helps you reconnect with your emotional experience, recognize feelings, and learn to express them safely. You'll learn that emotions aren't dangerous—they're information. When you can feel and express emotions, you can build deeper connections with others. Emotional awareness is the foundation of secure attachment. This module helps you build it.
takeaways: Emotions are information, not threats: they tell you what you need.
Suppressing emotions creates distance: expressing them creates connection.
Emotional awareness is a skill: you can learn to recognize and express feelings.
Vulnerability is strength: expressing emotions requires courage.
exercises: Emotion check-in: Three times today, pause and ask: 'What am I feeling right now?' Write it down. Notice patterns.
Body scan: Do a body scan. Notice physical sensations. What emotions might they be connected to?
Emotion identification: Use an emotion wheel to identify 5 different emotions you've felt this week. Write about each one.
homework: Daily emotion check-ins: Each day this week, check in with your emotions 3 times. Notice what you're feeling. Write it down.
Emotion journal: Keep an emotion journal. Track: What emotion? When? What triggered it? How did it feel in your body?
Emotion expression practice: Share one emotion with someone you trust this week. Start small. Notice how it feels.
Body awareness practice: Practice body scans daily. Notice physical sensations. Connect them to emotions.

modules.title: Module 3 • Challenging Avoidant Behaviors: Opening to Connection
modules.overview: Avoidant attachment involves specific behaviors: withdrawal, emotional suppression, self-reliance, and distancing. This module helps you identify these behaviors and challenge them. You'll learn to recognize when you're withdrawing, why you're doing it, and how to choose differently. You'll practice staying present in relationships even when it's uncomfortable. Changing behaviors changes relationships. When you can stay present instead of withdrawing, you can build deeper connections.
takeaways: Avoidant behaviors are patterns, not truths: you can choose differently.
Withdrawal creates distance: staying present creates connection.
Discomfort is temporary: the benefits of connection are lasting.
Small steps matter: you don't have to change everything at once.
exercises: Behavior audit: List 5 avoidant behaviors you notice in yourself. When do they appear? What triggers them?
Withdrawal awareness: This week, notice when you want to withdraw. Pause. Ask yourself: 'What am I feeling? What am I afraid of?'
Staying present practice: Choose one situation this week where you'd normally withdraw. Stay present instead. Notice what happens.
homework: Behavior tracking: Track your avoidant behaviors this week. When do they appear? What triggers them? How do you respond?
Withdrawal challenge: When you notice the urge to withdraw, practice staying present. Start with 5 minutes. Build from there.
Help-seeking practice: Ask for help with something small this week. Accept support when offered. Notice how it feels.
Emotional expression: Share one emotion with someone this week. Start small. Notice the response.

modules.title: Module 4 • Building Intimacy Skills: Learning to Be Close
modules.overview: Intimacy can feel threatening when you have avoidant attachment. This module helps you understand intimacy, build comfort with closeness, and develop skills for deeper connection. You'll learn that intimacy doesn't mean losing yourself—it means sharing yourself. You can be close and independent, connected and autonomous. Intimacy is a skill. You can learn it. This module shows you how.
takeaways: Intimacy is sharing yourself, not losing yourself: you can be close and independent.
Intimacy is built gradually: small steps create deeper connection.
Vulnerability is required: you can't have intimacy without it.
Intimacy is worth the risk: the benefits of connection outweigh the discomfort.
exercises: Intimacy assessment: How comfortable are you with intimacy? Rate yourself 1–10 in different areas: emotional, physical, intellectual, experiential.
Intimacy practice: Choose one small act of intimacy this week. Share a feeling. Spend time together. Notice how it feels.
Intimacy skills: Practice one intimacy skill this week: emotional sharing, active listening, empathy, vulnerability, or presence.
homework: Intimacy building: This week, practice one small act of intimacy daily. Start where you're comfortable. Build from there.
Intimacy skills practice: Practice intimacy skills this week. Share feelings. Listen actively. Be present. Notice the impact.
Balance practice: Practice balancing intimacy and independence. Spend time together and apart. Share and maintain boundaries.
Intimacy reflection: Reflect on your intimacy practice. What's comfortable? What's challenging? What would you like to try next?

modules.title: Module 5 • Building Trust: Learning to Depend on Others
modules.overview: Trust is difficult when you have avoidant attachment. You've learned that depending on others is unsafe. This module helps you build trust gradually, learn to depend on others appropriately, and develop secure relationships. You'll learn that trust doesn't mean blind faith—it means choosing to depend on others while maintaining your own strength. Trust is a skill. You can learn it. This module shows you how.
takeaways: Trust is earned gradually: you don't have to trust everyone immediately.
Trust doesn't mean losing yourself: you can depend on others and still be strong.
Small acts of trust build bigger trust: start small and build from there.
Trust is worth the risk: the benefits of connection outweigh the fear.
exercises: Trust assessment: How much do you trust others? Rate yourself 1–10. What makes trust difficult? What would help?
Trust practice: Choose one small act of trust this week. Share a feeling. Ask for help. Accept support. Notice how it feels.
Dependency practice: Practice depending on others this week. Ask for help. Accept support. Notice that you're still you.
homework: Trust building: This week, practice one small act of trust daily. Start where you're comfortable. Build from there.
Dependency practice: Practice depending on others this week. Ask for help. Accept support. Share problems. Notice the impact.
Trust reflection: Reflect on your trust practice. Who do you trust? Why? What would help you trust more?
Boundary and trust balance: Practice balancing trust and boundaries. Trust others while maintaining your strength.

modules.title: Module 6 • Secure Communication: Expressing Needs and Emotions
modules.overview: Avoidant attachment often involves difficulty expressing needs and emotions. This module teaches you to communicate clearly, express yourself authentically, and build connection through communication. You'll learn that expressing needs doesn't make you weak—it makes you human. You'll learn to communicate in ways that create connection rather than distance. Secure communication is a skill. You can learn it. This module shows you how.
takeaways: Expressing needs is healthy: it's human to have needs and express them.
Communication creates connection: sharing yourself builds relationships.
Vulnerability is strength: expressing yourself authentically requires courage.
Clear communication prevents problems: expressing needs directly avoids misunderstandings.
exercises: Need identification: List 5 needs you have. Which are easy to express? Which are difficult? Why?
Need expression practice: Practice expressing one need this week. Make it specific. Make it clear. Notice the response.
Emotion expression practice: Practice expressing one emotion this week. Name it. Share it. Notice how it feels.
homework: Need expression: This week, practice expressing needs. Start small. Make them specific. Notice how it feels.
Emotion expression: Practice expressing emotions this week. Name them. Share them. Notice the impact.
Active listening: Practice active listening in conversations. Give full attention. Reflect back. Ask questions.
Communication reflection: Reflect on your communication. What's easy? What's difficult? What would you like to improve?

modules.title: Module 7 • Building Secure Attachment: Integration and Maintenance
modules.overview: This final module helps you integrate everything you've learned into a sustainable practice of secure attachment. You'll create a plan for maintaining progress and continuing growth. You'll learn that secure attachment is a journey, not a destination. It requires ongoing practice, but it becomes easier over time. You'll develop confidence in your ability to maintain secure attachment patterns and build relationships that are both close and healthy.
takeaways: Secure attachment is a practice: it requires ongoing effort, but it becomes easier.
Progress isn't linear: setbacks are normal; return to the basics when they happen.
Support helps: don't do this alone—seek help when needed.
Celebrate progress: acknowledge how far you've come.
exercises: Progress reflection: Reflect on your journey. What have you learned? How have you grown? What's changed?
Maintenance plan: Create a plan for maintaining secure attachment. What will you do daily? Weekly? Monthly?
Future vision: Imagine your future with secure attachment. What does it look like? How do you feel? What's different?
homework: Integration plan: Create a plan for integrating secure attachment into your daily life. What practices will you maintain?
Support network: Identify your support network. Who can you turn to? How will you maintain connections?
Growth goals: Set 3 goals for continued growth. What will you work on? How will you measure progress?
Celebration: Celebrate your progress. Write about it. Share it. Acknowledge how far you've come.

aiSupport.systemPrompt: Help the user apply one concrete module step at a time. Do not diagnose. Escalate urgent safety concerns to emergency care.
